title: The week's rhythm
hookLine: weekday prayers, a weekend gurdwara, a weekly seva
tomorrow: what do you pray for a child who isn't born yet?

lines: A SHAPE TO CARRY IT IN.
cards: Sunday night, a calendar app: color blocks for school, work, practice, a birthday, the dentist. Every block is a promise to someone.
Sikhs who keep the full rhythm add a few blocks that don't move: the daily banis, a weekend visit to the gurdwara, a regular stretch of seva. Not more to carry. A shape to carry it in.

teach.b: Start with the daily part: the banis at dawn and dusk and bedtime, the same words at the same doors.
Then the weekly part, with other people. The sangat, the congregation. Guru Nanak asks, on ang 72, in paraphrase: how is the true congregation known?
Where the One Name is spoken. Not by its size, or its building. Then seva, service done without pay: the langar kitchen, the shoe room, sweeping, washing dishes.

teach.h: SEVA, IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORLD.
teach.b: On ang 26 Guru Nanak puts it plainly, in paraphrase: do seva in the middle of the world, and you'll find a place in the Lord's court. In the middle of the world, not after it.
So what does the tradition give you for a crowded week?
A rhythm, not a pile. A pile grows every time you add to it, and one missed day makes it feel ruined. A rhythm is a pattern you come back to.
It bends in a hard week, a sick week, a week with a baby coming, and it still beats. Daily words, a weekly gathering, a regular piece of service.

how: Sikhs who keep the full rhythm say the daily banis morning and evening, join the sangat at the gurdwara, often at a weekend diwan, and take a regular share of seva, in the langar, the shoe room or cleaning.

o: a fixed list of fasts kept on certain weekdays
daily banis, weekly sangat and regular seva, as a pattern
one day a week set aside for visiting family

games.q: a week's rhythm — tap the pairs.
p: the banis at dawn, dusk and bedtime
where the One Name is spoken

s: Guru Nanak says the true congregation is known by its size
ang 72: it's known as the place where the One Name is spoken.
on ang 26, seva is done in the middle of the world
not after it: do seva here, and find a place in the Lord's court.
miss one day and a rhythm is broken
a rhythm is a pattern you come back to; it bends and still beats.

games.q: your friend builds a perfect week of prayer and service, misses Tuesday, and wants to quit. what does a rhythm offer her?
o: pick it up on Wednesday; a rhythm is the coming back, not a perfect streak.
start the whole plan over next Monday so the week counts from the beginning.
double Wednesday's prayers so the week's total still comes out the same.
games.why: a pile feels ruined by one missed day; a rhythm bends and still beats.

practice: Open the coming week in your head. Choose one fixed time for prayer, one for gathering with others, and one for service. For each, name the thing most likely to crowd it out, and what you'll do when it does.

wordCard.voice: The week's rhythm. Daily banis, a weekly sangat, and regular seva, kept as a pattern you come back to.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sangat, the congregation: where the One Name is spoken.

carryVoice: Your line: a rhythm for the week. It bends, and it still beats. Have a good one.
